# S-1 · Control Selection

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | S Select (system level) |
| Phases | PH-TMRR (primary) |
| Depends on | C-3, P-5 |
| Inputs | ART-CAT, ART-BIA, ART-ORG-CONTEXT, ART-REQ, EXT-BASELINES, EXT-CNSSI1253-OVERLAYS, EXT-CATALOG, ART-INV, ART-RA, EXT-ORG-POLICY |
| Outputs | ART-BASELINE (produces) |
| Writes facts | baseline_id |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-PM, PER-CCP, PER-ISSM · A: PER-PM · C: PER-AO, PER-IO, PER-ISSE, PER-PRIV, PER-ISSO · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-CCP](../../personas/PER-CCP.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-ISSO](../../personas/PER-ISSO.md) |

Purpose: Select the NSS control baseline in CNSSI 1253 Appendix D that matches the approved C/I/A categorization, plus the NSS privacy baseline, as the starting point for tailoring.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** `facts.yaml#categorization.approved.value` is `true` with
   `set_by_task: C-3`. If not, stop: `rmf baseline resolve` refuses an unapproved
   categorization, and FACTS-001 fails. Why: controls are selected from the approved
   categorization only (DoDI 8510.01 Table 3, CNSSI 1253 §3.2.1).
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs` and the selection procedure:
   `uv run rmf refs show CNSSI1253 --section "3.2.1"` and
   `uv run rmf refs show SP800-53B --section "2.2"`.
3. **Interview** PER-ISSM, then PER-CCP (`## Interviews`). The ISSM confirms the baseline and
   overlays follow from the approved categorization; the common control provider says which
   of its common controls the system may inherit, fully or in part.
4. **Resolve the baseline.** Run `uv run rmf baseline resolve <run>`. It reads only
   `facts.yaml` (categorization and overlays), `run.yaml` (`control_subset`, if any), and any
   `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml` add/remove actions, and writes `baseline.json`. Never edit
   `baseline.json` (INV-2). The tool applies CNSSI 1253 per-objective selection
   (`method: cnssi1253`): the union of the Appendix D controls selected at the confidentiality,
   integrity and availability levels of the categorization, plus the NSS privacy control
   baseline, which CNSSI 1253 §3.2.1 makes a default for all NSS, then the listed overlays
   (a Privacy Overlay set chosen by the privacy risk level, which replaces the PCIL; C-2 step 6),
   tailoring and `control_subset`. Only when CNSSI 1253 is recorded as degraded does it fall
   back to the SP 800-53B high-water mark (`method: high-water-mark`). Why it matters: the
   artifact must describe the baseline the tool actually produced, so read `method` and
   `baseline_id` from `baseline.json`.
5. **Write the baseline fact.** Read `baseline_id` from the new `baseline.json`, then rewrite
   `facts.yaml` whole, keeping every field, and set:

   ```yaml
   baseline_id:
     value: CNSSI1253-M-M-L-SUBSET-6
     set_by_task: S-1
     sources: [INT-010.A1]
   ```

   The value is exactly the `baseline_id` in `baseline.json`. Why: the facts block and the
   OSCAL SSP show the baseline from `facts.yaml`; a value that differs from `baseline.json`
   would contradict the generated profile.
6. **Leave tailoring and allocation alone.** `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml` (S-2) and
   `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml` (S-3) belong to other tasks; when they are seeded, read
   them but do not change them. Why: S-1 selects; tailoring and allocation are their own
   decisions with their own owners.
   Then check the resolved set: no control enhancement is selected without its base control
   (TLR-007); an enhancement adds to its base, never replaces it.
   **Map the capabilities, when the organization defined any.** If ART-ORG-CONTEXT or the
   ISSM names security or privacy capabilities defined ahead of selection (for example,
   secure remote authentication), write `artifacts/data/capabilities.yaml` whole (schema
   `capabilities`): one record per capability with every selected control that supports
   it. A control may support several capabilities. Every mapped control must be a catalog
   control (TLR-008), so a failed control can later be read against the capability it
   weakens. A mapped control the baseline does not select is a gap, a warning (TLR-011):
   note it for S-2 to weigh supplementation. Write no file when no capability is defined.
7. **Write `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md`:
   - selection basis: the method recorded in `baseline.json` (CNSSI 1253 per-objective
     selection plus the NSS privacy control baseline, or the SP 800-53B high-water mark if
     CNSSI 1253 is degraded) for the approved categorization in the facts block, plus the
     overlays it lists (do not retype the values). Name the method exactly as recorded;
   - common controls available for inheritance, per provider, from ART-ORG-CONTEXT and the
     CCP's answers;
   - tailoring and allocation: a short summary of what `tailoring.yaml` and
     `allocation.yaml` contain and who produced them (or that S-2/S-3 will), traced to the
     same tokens those files cite or to the answers;
   - any requirement in ART-REQ the baseline does not obviously cover, for S-2 to address.
8. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-1`,
   until 0 errors. `rmf build` also writes the OSCAL profile from `baseline.json`.
9. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-ISSM | responsible (R) | baseline and overlays implied by the approved categorization, organizational additions, requirements not covered |
| PER-CCP | responsible (R) | common controls the system may inherit, fully or as hybrid, and the provider's authorization status |
| PER-PM (optional) | accountable (A) | acceptance of the selected baseline, resources for system-specific controls |
| PER-PRIV (when the system processes PII) | consulted (C) | with PER-ISSM: the privacy controls of the NSS privacy baseline and the Privacy Overlay control set, and privacy requirements of ART-REQ the baseline does not cover |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects PER-ISSM and PER-CCP interviews.

## Inputs

- `facts.yaml` (`categorization`, with `approved`)
- `artifacts/ART-CAT.md`
- `artifacts/ART-ORG-CONTEXT.md` (common controls, organizational tailoring)
- `artifacts/ART-REQ.md`
- `artifacts/data/tailoring.yaml`, `artifacts/data/allocation.yaml` (read only, when present)
- References: CNSSI1253 §3.2.1, SP800-53B §2.2

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline.json` | — | generated by `rmf baseline resolve` |
| `artifacts/ART-BASELINE.md` | `artifact_id: ART-BASELINE`, `produced_by_task: S-1`, `touched_by: [S-1]` | S-2 and S-3 append themselves when they run |
| `facts.yaml` | — | `baseline_id` only |

## Facts

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline_id` | `baseline_id` from `baseline.json` | the ISSM's confirmation |

## Done when

- `baseline.json` is current (GEN-STALE-001) and `facts.yaml#baseline_id` equals its
  `baseline_id`, with `set_by_task: S-1`.
- ART-BASELINE records the selection basis and the common controls available.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task S-1` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task S-1`, with the baseline ID and control count.
- If `rmf baseline resolve` refused (for example an unapproved categorization), that is a
  stop condition, not something to work around: journal a NOTE.
